approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Public field-type configuration keys and their meanings form a compatibility contract with remote consumers such as Rock Mobile, so changing them can break existing clients.

An Obsidian grid CopyColumn renders a button that copies text to the browser clipboard; it uses the row value identified by the column's field setting unless valueToCopy is supplied to compute the text from the row, column definition, and grid state.
BooleanColumn uses defaults for the standard formatComponent and exportValue properties and does not introduce any column-specific properties.
In an Obsidian grid, SelectColumn renders row-selection checkboxes that allow grid actions to operate on multiple selected rows.

An Obsidian block requires a C# server component for its logic, while its client component supplies the user interface and may be omitted for a web block that only returns static HTML without interactions.

In an Obsidian grid, DateColumn renders the value of its configured field as a short-form date and supplies defaults for formatting, skeleton display, quick-filter values, and exported values; it adds no column-specific properties.
The Obsidian Browser Bus is a page-local publish-subscribe mechanism backed by DOM events; its messages do not cross browser tabs or reach another user's browser.

When an Obsidian field type uses different public display and edit representations, its client-side value-formatting methods must accept either representation because an unsaved edit component value can be supplied where the display representation is normally expected.

For an Obsidian plugin, `npm run build` performs TypeScript type checking before compiling and copying assets to RockWeb, whereas `npm run watch` continuously recompiles changed files without type checking.
Obsidian block actions are stateless server calls, so every action must revalidate client data and recheck authorization rather than relying on TypeScript visibility or a previous C# instance.

Generated detail-block save handlers initially treat every selected property as writable, so properties included only to control the UI, such as IsSystem, must be removed from the saveable-property list to prevent unintended database updates.
Set an Obsidian Grid's key field to the data property that uniquely identifies each row when using advanced grid features that depend on row identity.
Obsidian block clients exchange JSON data with their C# server component and invoke block actions through endpoints that retain the block's settings and normal security enforcement.
An Obsidian grid LabelColumn can translate raw field values into display text with textSource, then use that translated text as the lookup key for classSource or colorSource styling.

A Universal Field Type keeps UI code outside its C# field-type implementation and supplies structured data for the client framework to render; item, tree, and search picker implementations using this pattern also receive Data View filtering support.

When NumberBadgeColumn ranges overlap, the effective precedence from highest to lowest is danger, warning, success, info, then hidden; therefore a matching color range can override a configured hide range.
The Obsidian grid SecurityColumn displays a per-row control that opens Rock's standard security editor for the corresponding item.
Attaching the VS Code debugger to an existing Chrome session requires Chrome to be launched with remote debugging enabled on port 9222.
Obsidian's NumberBadgeColumn displays a number in a badge and selects its color by testing the value against configured inclusive minimum and maximum ranges.
PersonColumn can link a displayed person to the person detail page, but it does not verify that the viewer is authorized to access that page; the documented showAsLink behavior is scoped to Rock 17.

After ReorderColumn updates the grid's row order, its optional onOrderChanged callback receives the moved row and the row now following it, or null when moved to the end; the callback can persist the change, return false to cancel it, or return a promise that blocks further reordering until completion.

Every Obsidian detail block should enforce either entity security, which authorizes against the displayed entity, or CMS security, which uses the block's permissions; when replacing an unsecured WebForms detail block, start with CMS security and review the effective page permissions.
In an Obsidian grid, a generic Column can display custom cell content by defining the format template and using its row value to render the desired markup.
AttributeColumns does not support the standard grid column properties, but it can be configured with an attribute filter and a skeleton component shown while grid data is loading.

An Obsidian field type must convert private field and configuration data into transmission-safe public representations; identifiers may also be expanded into client-friendly objects when the client needs additional display data, with a corresponding conversion back to the stored representation.
The Rock VS Code workspace provides separate debugger configurations for the Obsidian Framework and Obsidian Blocks projects, with options to launch a new browser or attach to an existing one.

In a rock-dev-tool setup, the development environment owns the runnable Rock installation and selected Rock version, while each plugin remains a separate source repository that can be attached to multiple environments for testing against different Rock versions.
Values whose changes must update an Obsidian component's template should use reactive ref or computed values; changing an ordinary variable does not notify the template to render again.

The Obsidian grid EditColumn invokes its optional click callback with the row key; the callback may be synchronous or return a Promise, in which case the edit button stays disabled until that Promise settles.

An Obsidian grid ButtonColumn renders one icon button and requires both an icon CSS class and a click handler; the handler receives the row key and current grid state and may complete synchronously or asynchronously.
SecurityColumn uses the row's "isSecurityDisabled" field by default to disable its security control when that field is true; a different row field can be selected through disabledField.
RockFieldColumn requires an attribute definition, which it uses to format the field value for display.
An Obsidian grid custom column filter combines a popup component that constructs the filter value with a predicate function that receives each row and that value to decide whether the row matches.

An Obsidian block can grant child controls scoped API access by creating a server-side security grant, sending its token in block configuration, providing that grant in the client component tree, and including the injected token in control API requests; the block should expose token renewal because these tokens expire after one hour by default.
The Obsidian grid DateTimeColumn formats a cell as a short date and time, showing the date, hour, and minutes by default; setting showSeconds to true adds seconds.

In an Obsidian grid, HighlightDetailColumn renders its primary field in bold and can render a secondary row-property value beneath it when detailField names that property; omitting detailField or setting it to false leaves the secondary area empty.

For most Obsidian pickers, `showBlankItem` controls whether a selected value can be cleared, while the `required` validation rule independently controls whether the form can be submitted without a value.
In an Obsidian grid, BooleanColumn renders a checkmark when its bound value is true and leaves the cell empty otherwise.
Obsidian developer documentation may describe core-only patterns; plugin developers should apply a documented pattern only after determining that it also applies to plugins.

Plugin endpoints that supply Universal Tree Item Picker or Search Picker data should accept POST input from the request body and use an `api/v2/plugins/{organization-code}/...` route; the `api/v2` prefix produces the camel-cased response properties expected by Obsidian clients, while the organization segment avoids plugin route collisions.

Obsidian's `cachePromise` utility wraps a Promise-returning operation so concurrent calls with the same wrapper reuse the in-flight Promise, and later calls reuse the serialized result until its expiration time; the default expiration is one minute.
DeleteColumn can disable deletion per row through rowDisabled, and when its onClick callback returns a Promise, the delete button stays disabled until that Promise resolves.
For core Obsidian development, the Code Generator can scaffold a basic list block that can then be customized; this generator is not available for plugin blocks.

Obsidian grids provide standard column filters for boolean, date, numeric, and text values, plus a filter that lets a person select one or more values from the column's unique existing values; the text filter uses substring matching.

In an Obsidian TypeScript model for JSON data, declare a property as optional when the server may omit it, and include `null` in its type when the server may also send an explicit null value; for example, a nullable string that may be omitted should use `property?: string | null`.
The Obsidian developer documentation is a work in progress, so described behavior may change or may not yet be implemented as documented.

In an Obsidian grid column, the format, condensed, header, and skeleton templates take precedence over their corresponding rendering component properties; condensedComponent falls back to formatComponent when no condensed component is specified.
Obsidian TypeScript code should import across packages with aliases such as `@Obsidian/...`; relative imports are reserved for files in the same package or directory.

Obsidian grids perform filtering, sorting, and paging in the browser, so the complete row set must be transferred before rendering; configuring a smaller page size does not reduce the amount of data sent to the client.

In an Obsidian grid, the AttributeColumns placeholder determines where dynamically generated columns for entity attribute values are inserted; its attributes property accepts the attribute definitions to display.

A Person grid that does not inherit from RockListBlockType must provide block actions for creating entity sets and communications, and its grid definition must identify a Person key field using an IdKey or GUID, for the corresponding default grid actions to work.
An Obsidian Grid can receive its required data directly or through a function; if that function returns a promise, the grid waits asynchronously for the result.
Obsidian's ReorderColumn renders a drag handle that lets a user move a row to a different position in the grid.
In an Obsidian grid, CurrencyColumn formats the cell value as currency and supplies default formatting, loading-skeleton, and export-value behavior without adding column-specific properties.
An Obsidian grid using PersonColumn must add its person field through AddPersonField() so the column receives all values required to render the person.

Core Obsidian additions must respect the package dependency hierarchy: a package may depend on packages above it in the hierarchy, but dependencies must not create direct or indirect cycles; block developers may import from any of the documented Obsidian packages.

In older Obsidian `.ts` files, a Vue compiler error reported only as `SyntaxError 15` indicates that whitespace is missing between attributes; this numeric-error troubleshooting issue is not expected for newer `.obs` files.

To make a core field type available in Obsidian, declare Obsidian platform support on its C# field type, expose its GUID through the generated field-type system GUIDs, and import and register its TypeScript implementation in the Obsidian field-type index.

To cache an Obsidian API request, import the cache utility from `@Obsidian/Utility/cache`, call `cachePromise` with a unique cache key, a function that returns the request Promise, and optionally an expiration time, then invoke the returned function instead of issuing the request directly.

A control API endpoint that accepts a security-grant token must reconstruct and evaluate the grant alongside the current person's normal authorization; unauthorized single-entity operations should return an unauthorized response, while list operations should omit entities the caller cannot access, using the authorization action appropriate to the operation.
In an Obsidian grid, TextColumn renders the field value as plain text and introduces no properties beyond the standard column properties.

An Obsidian block can provide a custom configuration screen by implementing `IHasCustomActions`, returning an administrate-only action whose component URL points to a separate `.obs` template, and exposing block actions to load and save the custom settings.
In an Obsidian component, a property's default is used only when the parent omits that property; explicitly passing null preserves null instead of substituting the default.

An Obsidian RockForm can be submitted by binding its submit prop and setting the bound value to true; after validation completes, the form resets that value to false and emits the submit event only when submission may proceed.
A JavaScript truthiness check rejects `undefined`, `null`, and an empty string together; use explicit comparisons instead when an Obsidian component must distinguish among those states.
The Obsidian grid DeleteColumn asks for confirmation before invoking its click handler by default; setting disableConfirmation to true bypasses that prompt.

Core `.obs` development is supported in Visual Studio Code rather than the Visual Studio editor, and the repository workspace supplies the expected settings and watch tasks for Obsidian controls and blocks.

Add an EditColumn to an Obsidian grid and assign its click handler to provide a per-row edit action; the column supplies defaults for its name, formatter component, header and item classes, and width.
LabelColumn styling can be configured either with classSource values that identify standard label suffixes or with colorSource values that specify CSS background colors.

In an Obsidian RockForm, input components report rule-validation results through their internal RockFormField; when the nearest form is submitted, RockForm blocks submission and displays its standard validation notice if any field is invalid, otherwise it emits the submit event.
The Obsidian grid NumberColumn formats numeric cell values using the browser's current locale, including its thousands and decimal separators.
RockFieldColumn is an internal Rock grid column for displaying one Rock field value and should not be used by plugins.
An Obsidian grid column can remain available to exports or other processing while hidden on screen with hideOnScreen, whereas excludeFromExport removes the column from export output.

An Obsidian field configuration change handled entirely in the client should emit an updated model value, while a change that requires refreshed server-derived options should additionally request a configuration update.
